## 1. Brief

**What it is.** Upcreate (earlier names: chillchai, then Upforge Content OS) is a personal content operating system for Shardul / Upforge. Upforge is a market-entry and business-consulting practice for MSMEs, with 30+ clients across 15 industries and 6 countries. Shardul started consulting at 18–19 after failing his entrance exams.

The app turns an Instagram growth-blueprint playbook into working tools for planning, researching, scripting, producing, publishing and measuring short-form content. The playbook covers hook stacks, 5x-outlier research, the 70/20/10 concept ratio, the authority/journey pillars, storytelling frameworks, and funnel-matched CTAs. The app also ships with a ready-to-film library: **1,000 reel scripts** and **100 carousels**.

**Status (14 Nov 2026).**
- The app is built and deploys on Vercel + Supabase. All 33 routes compile, there are 0 lint errors, and the last code change was on 7 Oct.
- Most features are real and backed by the database.
- Publish, Media Bank, Version History, the ⌘K palette and the Settings modal show sample data only.

**Core design principle.** Every generator builds its full prompt from the user's brand config plus the playbook rules, **shows you the prompt**, and offers two buttons:
- **Generate**, using your connected AI provider
- **Copy prompt**, to paste into any chatbot

So nothing is locked behind an API key. The app is a thinking tool first and an AI wrapper second.

## 2. Features and the thinking behind them

The reasoning in this section comes from the commit history and the code comments.

### Overview

**Dashboard** (`/dashboard`)
- **What:** level progress, ratio meters (authority vs journey; proven / double-down / experimental), the upcoming batch, a Quickstart panel, and "Trending in your niche".
- **Why:** you open the app to answer "what do I film next, and am I keeping the ratio?". The trending reels come from your own logged outliers rather than a fake feed, so the dashboard never shows invented data.

### Plan

**Brand Foundation** (`/brand`)
- **What:** handle, niche, 9 sub-niches, occupation, founder story, colours, fonts, pillar ratio, concept ratio, posting cadence, hook and format preferences, CTA/ManyChat status, equipment, AI stack, "human alpha", proprietary value, journey assets, and the profile checklist (right vs wrong bio, link and handle).
- **Why:** this is the single source of truth that every prompt pulls from. Change your niche once and every generator, hook and caption changes with it. The config is cached in-process because nearly every page reads it and it rarely changes.

**Onboarding survey + Tour** (`/onboarding`)
- **What:** a skippable survey that seeds the brand config, then a skippable first-run tour of the app.
- **Why:** added for multi-user use. A new account starts with an empty brand rather than Shardul's, so the survey gives the generators context from day one.

**Calendar** (`/calendar`)
- **What:** a month grid; click any day to schedule any script.
- **Also:**
  - quick stats: total, posted, due this week, overdue, next up
  - filters: status, pillar, funnel, effort, topic, segment, search
  - 14 one-click batch imports
  - Word export
  - a Danger-zone reset
- **Why:** the first design was a flat list, which became unusable at 395+ items. A month-grouped redesign followed, and then a real mobile-style month grid. Scripts are linked to calendar rows by `script_id`, so the plan stays accurate as the library grows. Reset clears dates but never deletes scripts, so you can re-plan from scratch without losing written content. Imports are idempotent, and each batch was checked for "distinct dates = row count", which once caught a 28-date collision before it shipped.

**Pipeline** (`/pipeline`)
- **What:** a kanban board of calendar items by status (idea → researched → scripted → filmed → edited → posted).
- **Why:** the calendar answers *when*; the pipeline answers *where is it stuck*. Status changes are saved to the same data.

**Outlier Research** (`/research`)
- **What:**
  - a log of outliers, with the multiple of views over followers calculated automatically
  - a used/unused toggle
  - a CSV/TSV bulk import that auto-detects the columns
  - a keyword-bank generator
- **Why:** this is the playbook's 5x rule: a reel from a small or midsize creator that got at least 5x their follower count in views counts as "proven". Model those, not random ideas. The bulk import exists because typing outliers in one at a time was the bottleneck. You paste a creator's reels-by-views export (from the Sort Feed extension), preview the computed multiples, and bulk-insert only the outliers.
- **Note:** the "Auto-discovery preview" panel is sample data and is labelled "example". It shows what a future scraping integration would look like.

### Create

**Hook Lab** (`/hooks`)
- **What:** a hook-stack generator and library, the 7 hook angles, and universal cross-niche hook templates.
- **Why:** the hook decides reach. A "hook stack" (verbal + visual + text hook) gets designed before the script.

**Scripts → Write** (`/scripts`)
- **What:**
  - generators for authority/educational and storytelling scripts, with a **reach-vs-conversion depth control**
  - a funnel and CTA picker
  - **transcript → template** (turn a viral transcript into a fill-in-the-blank template)
  - the signature **"How to Enter an Industry"** series builder
  - a script bank, bulk import, and Word export
- **Why:**
  - **Depth control:** the playbook shows 1M views can mean 200 followers or 30K followers depending on depth, so depth is a choice you make.
  - **Funnel bug fix:** the funnel and CTA dropdowns were once silently ignored by the prompt. Fixing that made each stage produce genuinely different instructions.
  - **Prompt structure:** the core prompt uses *agentic single-prompt scaffolding*: retention plan → draft v1 → self-critique (the model switches role to "ruthless editor reviewing a stranger's draft") → final script. Hard constraints (5 or fewer) are kept separate from soft style guidelines, because research shows models follow constraints much less reliably past about 7–10 flat rules.
  - **Script layers:** every script has three colour-coded layers: **black = what to say, red = filming and camera direction, green = on-screen text and edit notes**.

**Scripts → Improve** (`/improve`)
- **What:** pick or paste a script, then run diagnose → prioritise → targeted rewrite. Includes script search and the full reference guide inline.
- **Why:** blind regeneration throws away lines that already work. The prompt lists weaknesses with severity, *protects strong lines*, fixes in order of severity, then re-checks against the craft rules. It can also suggest switching to a different format, angle, funnel stage or CTA, not just polish.
- **Note:** the Version History panel is sample data.

**Scripts → Library** (`/library`)
- **What:** all scripts with filters (funnel, effort, topic, segment, content type, pillar), search, expandable bodies, add-to-calendar, and bulk import.
- **Why:** with 1,000 scripts you need to *find* the right one. Topic, segment and effort were promoted from free-text notes to real database columns so they can be filtered. Script bodies load only when expanded, and the list loads 40 at a time, because shipping every body on every page view was about 1–2 MB per visit.

**Bulk script import** (Scripts and Library)
- **What:** paste up to 50 scripts separated by `---`. One AI call classifies them all (pillar, type, angle, format, CTA, funnel, effort, topic, segment).
- **Why:** this brings scripts you wrote outside the app into the same structure. Without an AI key it falls back to safe defaults, so the import never fails.

**Carousels → Create** (`/carousels`) and **→ Library** (`/carousel-library`)
- **What:** a slide-by-slide carousel builder and generator, plus a filterable library with lazy-loaded slides and 3 batch imports.
- **Why:** carousels are a second content type that drives saves, so they follow the same discipline as scripts: 8 archetypes and craft rules researched for carousels. Background *photos* were deliberately deferred because Shardul wants real stock photos, not AI images. Each carousel still records its background category so photo sourcing can be added later without a schema change.

**Production → Planner** (`/production`)
- **What:** the 12 filming formats, an equipment checklist, a shot list built from a saved script, and a batch folder namer.
- **Why:** batch filming needs a shot list per script and consistent folder names so editors can find footage.

**Production → Media Bank** (`/media`)
- **Status:** sample data only, intended as a footage and image library linked to scripts. No file-storage backend exists yet.

**Prompt Library** (`/prompts`)
- **What:** every generator can be run inline:
  - bio
  - keyword bank
  - topic and problem research
  - raw-idea → brief
  - outlier deconstruction
  - hooks and captions
  - ManyChat DM writer
  - calendar ideation
  - double-down
- **Also:** the full static reference library and a Word export of everything, filled in with your brand.
- **Why:** one place to run or print any prompt, or hand it to an editor or VA.

### Grow

**Publish** (`/publish`)
- **Status:** sample data only. It is meant to be a queue, a published list, and best posting times per platform. No posting backend exists yet, and the page copy currently over-claims.

**CTA & Funnel** (`/funnel`)
- **What:** the TOFU/MOFU/BOFU distribution, a CTA decision guide, a ManyChat setup checklist, and a caption generator.
- **Why:** the CTA must match intent. TOFU asks for a follow, MOFU offers value for a comment, and BOFU sends people to a ManyChat keyword or link. Using the same CTA everywhere reads as fluff.

**Analytics → Performance** (`/analytics`)
- **What:** log posted videos, see the top and bottom 5, and generate **double-down** variants of winners.
- **Why:** this closes the loop. The "double-down" 20% of the ratio is supposed to come from here.

**Analytics → Insights** (`/insights`)
- **What:** what's working and what to make next, built from real hooks and posts data.
- **Why:** fabricated "recommendations" were deliberately removed during the redesign.

### System

**Settings** (`/settings`)
- **What:** choose an AI provider (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), paste a key, and optionally override the model. The key is shown masked.
- **Why:** replaces the original hard-coded Gemini key. You can switch providers or rotate keys with no redeploy, and real provider errors are shown in the UI.

**Accounts**
- **What:** signup and login with scrypt password hashing and a signed 30-day cookie. Every query is scoped per user. The first account to sign up claims existing data that has no owner.
- **Why:** this moved the app from a single shared password to multiple users, so it can serve more than one creator.

**Word export**
- **What:** export one script, all scripts, the calendar, or the whole prompt library.
- **Why:** for printing, annotating, and handing work to editors.

## 3. UI style and design system

The current UI is a port of the `samarnasir/upcreate_fork` redesign, completed on 6–7 Oct 2026.

- **Mood:** "Perk-style": electric lime on warm parchment. Calm, editorial, lots of whitespace, soft rounded cards, a single loud accent.
- **Type:** **Geist** everywhere, in weights 400, 500, 600 and 700. Headings use weight 500 with tight tracking (`letter-spacing: -0.03em`). Page titles are 44px on desktop and 30px on mobile, with `leading-[1.05]`. The landing page adds **Inter Variable** (600) and **Instrument Serif italic** for a mixed sans and serif tagline.

**Colour tokens** (CSS variables, with light and dark themes):

| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--background` | `#ffffff` | `#14140f` | page |
| `--foreground` | `#14140f` | `#f5f5eb` | text |
| `--muted` | `#6e6e64` | `#a3a397` | secondary text |
| `--card` | `#f5f5eb` (parchment) | `#1e1e19` | cards |
| `--surface` | `#ffffff` | `#26261f` | inputs, inner panels |
| `--ash` | `#d2d2c8` | `#3a3a33` | input borders |
| `--charcoal` | `#30302a` | `#30302a` | warn badges |
| `--accent` | `#beff50` (lime) | `#beff50` | primary buttons, active states, selection, "current" pills |
| `--accent-deep` | `#14140f` | `#14140f` | text on lime |

**Shapes:**
- Cards: `rounded-[28px]`, `bg-card`, `p-6 md:p-7`
- Reel thumbnails: `rounded-[18px]`
- Inner rows: `rounded-[14px]`
- Inputs: `8px`
- Buttons, badges and tabs: fully rounded pills (`rounded-full`)
- Borders: hairlines at 15% opacity (`border-border/15`)

**Components** (`app/components/ui.tsx`):
- `Card` and `PageSection`
- `SectionHeader` (large title plus a muted description)
- `Badge` (default, accent, or warn)
- `Stat`
- `SubTabs` (pill tabs over a hairline divider)
- `DeleteForm`
- `ReelCard`: a 9:16 reel mock with gradient "footage", a subject silhouette, a hook overlay (caption, bold or split style), and a lime "Nx" outlier badge

**Motion:**
- Page sections fade up one after another (520 ms, `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`, 70 ms apart)
- Grid cards stagger in
- Pop-in for menus
- `grow-x` for progress bars
- A lime `pulse-dot` for live states
- A bell `ring`
- A slow `drift` for background blobs
- Colour transitions of 150 ms on links and buttons

**Details:**
- Scrollbars are hidden everywhere, but content still scrolls
- Focus outline: 2px in the foreground colour
- Text selection is lime

**Layout and chrome:**
- Left sidebar on desktop, grouped as Overview / Plan / Create / Grow. Related pages share one sidebar entry with pill sub-tabs (Scripts: Write · Improve · Library).
- On mobile, a top bar plus a slide-in drawer
- Topbar: ⌘K command palette, help menu with the tour, settings modal, account email
- Content is capped at `max-w-7xl`

**Landing page (`/`):** full-bleed hero video with a 40% black scrim and an animated film-grain overlay. It shows the logo, the tagline, and two pill buttons: white "Sign in" and outlined "Create an account".

**Brand mark:** a "U" monogram with an upward arrow (an inline SVG that takes on the accent colour). The favicon is a blue rounded square with a white arrow-into-U and orange accent bars.

**Carousel visual defaults** (from the carousel rules in section 6):
- 1080×1350 canvas
- At most 2 font families
- Headlines 60–90px, body never below 28px
- Solid colour or gradient by default
- Photos need a 40–60% scrim

## 4. Architecture

- **Stack:** Next.js 16.3.6 (App Router, Turbopack, `proxy.ts` auth gate), React 19.2, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, Postgres via postgres.js (Supabase), `docx`, hosted on Vercel.
- **Data:** `lib/db.ts` → `ensureSchema()` creates or alters these tables idempotently on first query: `users`, `brand_config`, `calendar_items`, `outlier_research`, `hook_stacks`, `scripts`, `script_templates`, `ai_settings`, `own_posts`, `carousels`, `carousel_slides`. Every table has a `user_id`.
- **Logic:**
  - `lib/actions.ts`: all server actions, including the seed/isSeeded/action trio for each batch
  - `lib/prompts.ts`: prompt builders
  - `lib/reference.ts`: playbook rules
  - `lib/ai-providers.ts`, `lib/auth.ts`, `lib/brand.ts`, `lib/docx-export.ts`
- **Environment variables:** `DATABASE_URL` (required, even at build time), `SESSION_SECRET`, optional `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_MODEL`.

## 5. Known issues and next steps

**Content**
1. **42 duplicate reel titles.** Phases 1–6 repeat titles in the P7–P9 top-ups. They are marked ⚠ in section 8.
2. **Carousel #1 contradicts itself.** Its title says "5 Pricing Mistakes" but the hook and slides say 7.
3. **Concept mix is off-target.** The library is 987 proven / 0 double-down / 13 experimental, against a 70/20/10 target.
4. **No format variety in journey reels.** All 46 are Voiceover format.
5. **Inconsistent carousel tags.** Carousel topic and segment tags are free text and don't match each other.

**Product**

6. **Sample data shown without a label:** Publish (whose copy claims real posting), Media Bank, Version History, the ⌘K palette, and the Settings modal.
7. **Reset leaves imports locked.** After a calendar reset, batch imports stay marked as done.

**Security and operations**

8. **API keys stored as plain text** in `ai_settings`.
9. **Open signup** with no email verification and no password reset.
10. **Stale docs:** the README and `.env.example` are out of date.
11. **Missing build setting:** the Vercel preview build fails, most likely because the Preview environment has no `DATABASE_URL`.

**Technical debt**

12. **Repetitive seed code:** 15 copy-paste seed functions, about 1,400 lines that could be a single generic function.
13. **No migrations and no automated tests.**

## 6. Playbook rulebook

These are the rules every generator, script and carousel follows. They are exported unedited from `lib/reference.ts` and `lib/carousel-reference.ts`.

### Reels and scripts (`lib/reference.ts`)

#### AUTHORITY_CONTENT_FORMATS

- Step-by-step tutorials (frameworks, formulas, actionable processes)
- Comparisons (side-by-side methods, actions, products, services)
- Myth busting & common mistakes
- Do vs Don't (right vs wrong)
- Educational tips & hacks
- Q&A, rankings & tier lists
- Transformations (before/after for you or clients)
- Celebrity / brand fake case studies ("if I were hired by X")
- "Starting from scratch" fake case studies ("if I reset to zero")

#### CALENDAR_STATUSES

- idea
- researched
- scripted
- filmed
- edited
- posted

#### CONCEPT_BUCKETS

- proven
- double_down
- experimental

#### CONTENT_TYPES

- educational
- storytelling
- authority
- other

#### CTA_GUIDANCE

- **follow:** Default for TOFU reach plays and proven-concept videos -- ask for a follow, nothing else.

- **engagement:** "Comment X" plays -- good for MOFU when you want signal/interaction before a pitch.

- **manychat:** Trigger-word → automated DM with your one bio link. Best for BOFU lead generation.

- **none:** Pure value/brand exposure, no ask at all.

#### CTA_TYPES

- follow
- engagement
- manychat
- none

#### FILMING_FORMATS

- **name:** Talking Back & Forth · **description:** Smart character vs naive character dialogue.
- **name:** Visual Format · **description:** Teaching using props or physical visuals.
- **name:** Voiceover Format · **description:** Narrating over B-roll/images.
- **name:** Multitasking Format · **description:** Teaching while cooking, cleaning, doing another activity.
- **name:** Setting Changes · **description:** Switching locations across cuts.
- **name:** Shot / Angle Changes · **description:** Changing camera angle every ~2 seconds.
- **name:** Clone Format · **description:** Doubling yourself on screen for comparison.
- **name:** Whiteboard Format · **description:** Explaining concepts visually on a whiteboard.
- **name:** Q&A Format · **description:** Off-camera interviewer asking questions.
- **name:** Green Screen Format · **description:** Speaking with relevant background media.
- **name:** Reaction Format · **description:** Reacting to niche viral clips with expert commentary.
- **name:** Audio B-Roll + Text · **description:** Line-by-line images/videos changing every 1-3 seconds, paired with on-screen text and emotional background music -- no voiceover.

#### FIVE_X_OUTLIER_RULE

An outlier is a reel from a small-to-midsize creator that got at least 5x more views than their total follower count. That's the bar for 'proven' before you model it.

#### FUNNEL_GUIDANCE

**Tofu**

- **label:** TOFU (Top of funnel)

- **goal:** Reach a cold audience that doesn't know you yet.

- **instruction:** Open with your strongest, broadest-appeal hook. No hard ask -- the only job of this video is to earn a follow or a save. Don't reference your business/offer directly; let value speak for itself.

**Mofu**

- **label:** MOFU (Middle of funnel)

- **goal:** Deepen trust with people who already follow or have seen you before.

- **instruction:** Go one layer deeper than a TOFU video -- more specific, more personal, or more advanced. Use a soft engagement CTA (ask a question, "comment X") to generate signal before pitching anything.

**Bofu**

- **label:** BOFU (Bottom of funnel)

- **goal:** Convert a warm, ready audience into a lead or client.

- **instruction:** Speak directly to someone who already trusts you and is close to a decision. Use a strong, specific CTA (ManyChat trigger word, DM keyword, or a direct pitch) -- this is the video allowed to ask for something.

#### FUNNEL_STAGES

- tofu
- mofu
- bofu

#### HISTORICAL_MEDIA_TIP

Whenever it exists, use the actual photo or video from the time period you're talking about -- not a generic stand-in. Real historical media is what makes a storytelling video feel authentic instead of staged.

#### HOOK_STACK_EXAMPLES

- **niche:** styling / fashion · **written:** Hairstyle neckline guide · **verbal:** This is the best hairstyle for different tops · **visual:** Clone visual effect (multiple versions of yourself side by side)
- **niche:** styling / fashion · **written:** How to dress for your proportions · **verbal:** How to dress for your body type · **visual:** Drawn-on visuals and body-type labels over the frame
- **niche:** styling / fashion · **written:** Jeans for different body types · **verbal:** Try on jeans based on your body shape · **visual:** Three clones on screen, each in a different jean cut, labeled

#### JOURNEY_SERIES_FORMATS

- **name:** Daily Series · **description:** Daily progress updates tracking a specific goal ("Day 1 of completing X").
- **name:** Progress Update Series · **description:** Sporadic updates on ongoing projects or long-term goals.
- **name:** Lessons Series · **description:** One specific lesson learned per episode.
- **name:** Step-by-Step Series · **description:** Breaking down one stage of a multi-step project per episode.
- **name:** Number & Metric Updates · **description:** Transparent income/revenue/performance figures.
- **name:** Cost Breakdowns · **description:** Exact financial spend for building a product, business, or project.
- **name:** What I Would Do Differently · **description:** Reflecting on mistakes and takeaways after a business phase.

#### PILLARS

- authority
- journey

#### PROFILE_RIGHT_WRONG

- **field:** Link in bio · **wrong:** Linktree with multiple links (kills conversion up to 50%) · **right:** 1 single destination link (landing page or freebie)
- **field:** Username · **wrong:** Random or confusing handle · **right:** Your full personal name or business name
- **field:** Tagline / name field · **wrong:** Only your name · **right:** [Name] | [Searchable keyword / niche / occupation]
- **field:** Profile picture · **wrong:** Far-away shot, multiple people, busy background · **right:** Clear close-up headshot, solid background
- **field:** Bio structure · **wrong:** Messy, unstructured, ambiguous text · **right:** 4-line structured framework -- clear in 5 seconds

#### REACH_VS_CONVERSION_EXAMPLE

**Easy**

- **label:** Easy / low-effort (e.g. a rating reel)

- **views:** 1,000,000 views

- **result:** ~200 new followers

- **verdict:** High reach, close to zero conversion.

**Complex**

- **label:** Complex / high-effort (raw storytelling / hyper-educational breakdown)

- **views:** 1,000,000+ views

- **result:** 30,000+ new followers

- **verdict:** Same reach ballpark, 150x the conversion.

#### SCRIPT_ANGLES

- **name:** Framework / Formula / Acronym · **description:** Teach a repeatable step-by-step process, formula, or acronym. · **fillInTemplate:** Hook: [Bold claim/result] using my [X]-step framework. / 1. [Step 1] -- [one-line why it matters] / 2. [Step 2] -- [one-line why it matters] / 3. [Step 3] -- [one-line why it matters] / CTA: [Follow/Save] for [promise of more frameworks like this].
- **name:** Comparison · **description:** Side-by-side evaluation of two methods, products, or actions. · **fillInTemplate:** Hook: [Option A] vs [Option B] -- which one actually [desired outcome]? / Option A: [A] -- pros: [x], cons: [y] / Option B: [B] -- pros: [x], cons: [y] / Verdict: [which one wins and why, tied to your experience] / CTA: [Comment A or B / Follow for more comparisons]
- **name:** Myth Bust / Common Mistake · **description:** Disprove a widespread niche misconception or correct a frequent error. · **fillInTemplate:** Hook: Stop believing [common myth] -- it's costing you [consequence]. / Why it's wrong: [explanation with proof/experience] / What to do instead: [correct approach] / CTA: [Follow to unlearn more myths in X]
- **name:** Do vs Don't (Right vs Wrong) · **description:** Clear visual/verbal contrast of correct vs incorrect approaches. · **fillInTemplate:** Hook: [Topic] -- here's the right way vs the wrong way. / Wrong: [mistake] -- why it fails: [reason] / Right: [correct move] -- why it works: [reason] / CTA: [Follow for more do's and don'ts in X]
- **name:** Educational Tip / Hack · **description:** One highly specific, actionable tactical tip or rule of thumb. · **fillInTemplate:** Hook: One [niche] tip that [specific outcome] in [timeframe]. / The tip: [exact tactic] / Why it works: [mechanism/reasoning] / How to apply it: [concrete next step] / CTA: [Save this / Follow for more tips]
- **name:** Transformation · **description:** Before/after breakdown for you or a client/customer. · **fillInTemplate:** Hook: [Before state] to [after state] in [timeframe] -- here's exactly how. / Before: [starting point, specific numbers if possible] / What changed: [the 2-3 key moves] / After: [result, specific numbers] / CTA: [Follow if you want the same result / DM keyword for the process]
- **name:** Challenge · **description:** Complete or document a niche-relevant challenge on camera. · **fillInTemplate:** Hook: I'm going to [challenge] in [timeframe] -- here's day/attempt 1. / The rules: [constraints] / What happened: [progress/result] / What I learned: [takeaway] / CTA: [Follow to see how this ends]

#### SCRIPT_CRAFT_RULES

**Hook**

- Verbal hook must land by 1.0s -- no logo, no "hey guys," no brand name, no setup sentence before it.
- Hook sentence is one clause, one claim, ≤10 words.
- Use the specific-outcome pattern where possible: [bad number] → [good number] in [timeframe] using [thing]. Numbers beat vague claims.
- Combine at least 2 of: pattern interrupt, emotional spike, curiosity gap, self-relevance callout ("If you're a [specific audience]...").
- Never state that a topic will be discussed -- state the payoff or tension itself.

**Body**

- One idea per video. Every example/beat must serve the single hook's promise -- no digressions.
- Pattern-interrupt cadence every 7-10s for educational/consulting content (every 3-5s only for fast/punchy formats).
- Place a reinforcement beat (mid-video re-hook/reframe) at roughly 25-40% and 60-75% of runtime.
- Each body segment should close the prior open loop and immediately open a new one -- no flat beats.
- Cut on sight: throat-clearing openers ("So," "Okay so," "Today I want to talk about"), hedges ("just," "really," "very," "kind of," "I think," "basically"), redundant connectives ("in order to" → "to"), restated setup ("as I mentioned").
- Target 130-145 wpm baseline (slower end for consulting/educational density -- ideas need processing time).

**Cta**

- TOFU: no hard CTA, or one soft low-friction CTA at the very end only, tied to the video's specific topic (not generic "follow me"). Never interrupt pacing for a mid-video CTA on TOFU content.
- MOFU: one CTA, can land mid- or end-video, framed as a value exchange ("comment X and I'll send you the checklist") -- not a sales ask.
- BOFU: one explicit, specific CTA near the end naming the exact next step (link in bio, DM keyword, book a call). Never repeat/nag a CTA.
- Never reuse the same CTA wording across all three funnel stages -- mismatched CTA-to-intent reads as fluff and kills trust.

**Length**

- Runtime multiplier on script word count: talking-head/no b-roll ×0.95, mixed voiceover+b-roll ×0.85, visual-heavy/whiteboard/demo ×0.75 (at 130-145 wpm baseline).
- ~140-150 words for a tight 60s explainer; scale roughly linearly down to 35-75 words for a 15-30s reel.
- Narrow the idea before shortening artificially -- a fully-resolved narrow claim beats a padded vague one at any length.

#### CAROUSEL_CRAFT_RULES

**Slidecount**

- Sweet spot is 8-10 slides for most posts. 6-7 minimum, 12-20 only for deep guides/dense frameworks.
- Fewer slides = higher completion rate but less engagement surface. More slides = more save-worthy but every slide must earn the next swipe or completion rate collapses.

**Hook**

- Slide 1's promise must be legible in under 1 second -- treat it as a headline, not a warm-up. No logo-first opens.
- Combine at least 2 of: specific numbers, bold/contrarian claim, curiosity gap (withhold the 'what'), direct address ('you'), pattern interrupt.

**Body**

- One idea per slide. If a slide needs more than ~10 words at body size to make its point, split it into two slides rather than shrinking the font.
- Every middle slide's job is to earn the next swipe (open-loop pacing) -- sagging middle slides kill completion rate the same way a flat beat kills a video.
- Max 2 font families (one display/headline, one body/sans). Bold weight for headline, regular/medium for body.

**Design**

- Dark-on-light or light-on-dark only. Any text-over-photo needs a 40-60% scrim/overlay for legibility.
- Font sizing on a 1080x1350 canvas: headline 60-90px, section header 40-55px, body 28-36px (never below 28px -- cut text instead of shrinking), labels 20-26px.
- Solid brand color or gradient is the best-practice default: highest legibility, lowest production cost. Photo backgrounds are a secondary/supplementary treatment, not the default.

**Cta**

- One CTA per carousel -- never stack asks (save + share + comment + follow dilutes all of them).
- Tie the CTA to the content's goal: awareness -> share, trust/reference -> save, conversation -> tight comment prompt, conversion -> explicit next step.

**Mistakes**

- Weak/vague slide 1 -- payoff not legible in 1 second.
- Information overload per slide -- multiple ideas crammed together.
- Inconsistent branding -- too many fonts/colors, mixed image quality.
- Missing or stacked CTA.
- Sagging middle slides that don't each re-earn the next swipe.
- Low-legibility text-over-photo with no scrim/overlay.

#### CAROUSEL_CTA_GUIDANCE

- **save:** Highest-value ask (strongest algo signal, implies evergreen value): "Save this for [specific future use case]."

- **share:** Best for reach expansion: "Tag/send this to someone who [needs it]."

- **comment:** Works only with a tight, specific question: "Which step are you on -- comment [A/B/C]."

- **follow:** Reach-play CTA for pure awareness content, no deeper ask: "Follow for more [topic] breakdowns."

- **link:** Direct conversion ask for warm/BOFU audiences: "Link in bio for [specific next step]."

#### CAROUSEL_CTA_TYPES

- save
- share
- comment
- follow
- link

#### 1. 3 Levels of Market Research

*2026-10-07 · authority · educational · Educational Tip / Hack · Shot / Angle Changes · TOFU → follow · effort: low · proven*

**🗣 Say**

> Level 1: Googling your competitors. Everyone does this. It tells you nothing you can act on.
> Level 2: Interviewing 10 people in your target market. Better -- now you have real objections to solve for.
> Level 3: Running a $500 test campaign before you build anything. This is the only level that tells you if people will actually pay.
> Most founders stop at Level 1 and wonder why their launch flops.

**🎥 Film**

> Change camera angle every ~2 seconds as each level is introduced -- wide shot for L1, closer for L2, tightest for L3.
> Hold up one finger per level, count up on screen.

**🔤 On screen**

> On-screen text: "LEVEL 1 / 2 / 3" stamped as each is introduced.
> Bold on-screen number for "$500" when it appears.
> End card: "Which level are you actually at?"

**👉 CTA:** Follow for the exact interview questions I use at Level 2.

#### 2. Why Most MSMEs Fail Their First Market Entry (3-Step Framework)

*2026-10-14 · authority · educational · Framework / Formula / Acronym · Whiteboard Format · TOFU → follow · effort: default · proven*

**🗣 Say**

> 87% of the MSMEs I've audited make the same 3 mistakes entering a new market. Here's the framework that fixes all three.
> Step 1: Beachhead first. Pick ONE narrow segment to dominate before you touch a second. Spreading thin is the #1 killer, not competition.
> Step 2: Price for that market's purchasing power, not your home market's. I've seen founders lose 40% of potential customers on price alone.
> Step 3: Map your 3 closest local competitors before you launch, not after. If you can't name them, you're not ready.
> Get the beachhead segment right and steps 2 and 3 get dramatically easier.

**🎥 Film**

> Write each step on the whiteboard as you say it, numbered 1-2-3.
> Circle "87%" and underline "beachhead" for emphasis.

**🔤 On screen**

> On-screen text reinforcing each number (87%, 40%) as spoken.
> Zoom in on the whiteboard for the final 3-step recap.

**👉 CTA:** Follow for the full beachhead-selection checklist next week.

#### 3. Rate These 5 Market-Entry Mistakes 1-10

*2026-10-21 · authority · educational · Myth Bust / Common Mistake · Reaction Format · TOFU → follow · effort: low · experimental*

**🗣 Say**

> Mistake 1: launching in a new country with zero local partner. That's a 9 out of 10 -- it's killed more expansions than bad products ever have.
> Mistake 2: copy-pasting your home-market pricing. 7 out of 10 -- purchasing power isn't the same everywhere.
> Mistake 3: skipping the regulatory check. 10 out of 10. I've seen a 6-month launch delay from this alone.
> Mistake 4: no local competitor mapping. 6 out of 10 -- fixable fast if you catch it early.
> Mistake 5: underbudgeting for legal setup. 8 out of 10.

**🎥 Film**

> React to each clip/stat card with genuine reaction (wince, nod) as if watching real footage.
> Hold up a number card (or on-screen graphic) for each rating.

**🔤 On screen**

> Freeze-frame + rating number stamp after each line.

**👉 CTA:** Follow if you want the full regulatory checklist next.

#### 4. The Psychology Behind Why Customers Overpay for Local Brands

*2026-10-28 · authority · educational · Educational Tip / Hack · Voiceover Format · TOFU → follow · effort: default · proven*

**🗣 Say**

> There's a real psychological reason a local brand can charge more than a cheaper import -- and it isn't only "trust."
> It's called the mere-exposure effect: the more familiar something feels, the safer it feels to buy, even if nothing about the product changed.
> That's why a foreign brand's FIRST job in a new market isn't selling -- it's becoming familiar. Repetition before conversion.
> I've watched founders skip this and wonder why a technically-better product loses to a "worse" local option that's everywhere, full stop.
> If you're entering a new market, budget for familiarity first, sales second.

**🎥 Film**

> No on-camera talking -- voiceover only.
> Cut to relevant b-roll for each beat.

**🔤 On screen**

> B-roll: a busy local storefront, a repeated ad appearing multiple times, a side-by-side product comparison.
> On-screen text: "mere-exposure effect" defined briefly on screen.

**👉 CTA:** Follow -- more psychology behind buying decisions every week.

#### 9. How to Enter an Industry: Fashion & Retail (Ep. 4/5)

*2026-12-02 · authority · authority · Framework / Formula / Acronym · Whiteboard Format · MOFU → engagement · effort: high · proven · series: How to Enter an Industry*

**🗣 Say**

> Episode 4: Fashion and Retail -- the industry where trend-timing kills more launches than product quality ever does.
> The #1 killer: founders design a full collection before validating a single style with real local buyers, then discover the trend already peaked by the time they launch.
> The framework: launch with a 3-piece capsule, not a full collection -- test which piece sells before you commit inventory capital to the rest.

#### 20. The Framework I Use to Decide If a Market Is Worth Entering

*2027-02-17 · authority · educational · Framework / Formula / Acronym · Whiteboard Format · TOFU → follow · effort: default · proven*

**🗣 Say**

> Before I let a client spend a rupee on a new market, it has to pass 3 filters.
> Filter 1: Is the total addressable market at least 10x your current revenue? If not, the upside doesn't justify the risk.
> Filter 2: Can you reach that market through a channel you already understand? New market AND new channel at once is how most expansions die.
> Filter 3: Is there a regulatory or logistics reason this market is HARDER to enter than it looks? If yes, that's often the moat protecting it -- and your opportunity.
> Three filters. If a market fails even one, I tell clients to wait.

#### 34. The Finance Mistake That Kills Market Entry Budgets

*2027-05-26 · authority · educational · Educational Tip / Hack · Voiceover Format · TOFU → follow · effort: default · proven*

**🗣 Say**

> Most market-entry budgets die from one finance mistake, and it's not overspending.
> It's building a single budget for the whole launch instead of splitting it into a test tranche and a scale tranche.
> The test tranche should be small enough that losing all of it doesn't threaten the business -- its only job is proving the model works.
> The scale tranche only gets released once the test tranche proves a specific number: cost to acquire a customer below what that customer is worth.
> Founders who skip this split either spend too cautiously to ever learn anything, or bet the whole budget on an unproven model.

**🎥 Film**

> No on-camera talking -- voiceover only.
> Cut to relevant b-roll for each beat.

#### 48. Loss Aversion: Why 'Don't Miss Out' Beats 'Here's What You Get'

*2027-09-01 · authority · educational · Educational Tip / Hack · Whiteboard Format · MOFU → engagement · effort: default · proven · topic: Economic psychology*

**🗣 Say**

> People feel the pain of losing something roughly twice as strongly as the pleasure of gaining something equal -- that's loss aversion, and it changes how you should frame an offer.
> "Here's what you get" activates the gain side, which is weaker.
> "Here's what you're currently losing by not fixing this" activates the loss side, which is stronger.
> Same offer, different frame, different response rate.

#### 64. Psychology of Buying, Ep. 4/5: The Paradox of Choice

*2027-12-22 · authority · authority · Myth Bust / Common Mistake · Whiteboard Format · MOFU → engagement · effort: high · proven · series: Psychology of Buying · topic: Consumer psychology*

**🗣 Say**

> Episode 4: more options don't convert better -- they convert worse, past a point most founders blow right through.
> The research is consistent: 3 well-differentiated choices outconvert 10 similar ones, because more options raise the cognitive cost of deciding until people disengage instead.

#### 79. The Commitment Consistency Trick That Gets Clients to Follow Through

*2028-04-05 · authority · educational · Educational Tip / Hack · Voiceover Format · MOFU → engagement · effort: high · proven · topic: People psychology*

#### 111. The Framework for Structuring a Fair Consulting Retainer

*2028-11-15 · authority · authority · Framework / Formula / Acronym · Talking Back & Forth · BOFU → manychat · effort: high · proven · topic: Consulting industry insider takes*

#### 146. Kahneman's 'System 1' Explains Why Your Pricing Feels Wrong Even When the Math Is Right

*2029-07-18 · authority · educational · Educational Tip / Hack · Voiceover Format · TOFU → follow · effort: default · proven · source: Book concept + opinion — Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow*

**🗣 Say**

> In Thinking, Fast and Slow, Kahneman splits the mind into two systems: System 1, fast and instinctive, and System 2, slow and deliberate.
> Most pricing objections come from System 1 reacting to a number before System 2 has evaluated the value behind it.
> My take: don't fight System 1 with more logic. Slow the client down first -- walk through the value BEFORE the number, so System 2 gets a fair shot at overriding the instinctive flinch.
> That single sequencing change has moved more deals than any pricing justification I've ever written.

#### 149. Christensen's Disruption Theory Explains Why Your Best Clients Can Kill Your Best Ideas

#### 159. Asch's Conformity Experiments Explain Why One Confident Voice Can Move an Entire Room

*2029-10-17 · authority · educational · Educational Tip / Hack · Voiceover Format · TOFU → follow · effort: default · proven · source: Research study breakdown — Solomon Asch's classic conformity experiments*

**🗣 Say**

> My take: in a client meeting with multiple stakeholders, the first opinion stated in the room often becomes the group's opinion, correct or not -- which is exactly why I try to get the quietest person's real view before the loudest person anchors the room.

#### 193. 'Fortune Favors the Bold' Is Only Half True -- Loss Aversion Research Explains the Other Half

*2030-06-12 · authority · educational · Myth Bust / Common Mistake · Reaction Format · TOFU → follow · effort: default · proven · source: Old proverb vs modern data — The proverb "fortune favors the bold" vs prospect theory's findings on loss aversion*

**🗣 Say**

> "Fortune favors the bold" gets used to justify almost any big, risky move.
> Loss aversion research shows boldness only pays off when the downside is genuinely survivable -- a bold bet that risks ruin isn't brave, it's only gambling with the whole business.
> My take: the useful version is "fortune favors bold bets with a survivable downside" -- less catchy, considerably more accurate, and the one I actually apply.

#### 194. 'Don't Put All Your Eggs in One Basket' -- Buffett's Own Track Record Actually Argues the Opposite

*2030-06-19 · authority · authority · Comparison · Whiteboard Format · MOFU → engagement · effort: high · proven · source: Old proverb vs modern data — The proverb "don't put all your eggs in one basket" vs Buffett's concentrated-investing counterpoint*

**🗣 Say**

> "Don't put all your eggs in one basket" is treated as universal risk-management wisdom.
> Buffett has argued the opposite for genuine experts: watch that one basket closely and concentrate on what you deeply understand, rather than diluting attention across many baskets you understand less well.
> My take: diversification protects you from what you don't understand. Concentration rewards you for what you understand deeply. The proverb is right for a generalist -- it's actually costly advice for a specialist.
> Know honestly which one you are in your niche before deciding which advice applies.
> Comment "BASKET" and I'll send you how I decide when to concentrate vs diversify client focus.

#### 195. 'First Impressions Last' Isn't Just Folk Wisdom -- Halo Effect Research Explains the Mechanism

*2030-06-26 · authority · educational · Educational Tip / Hack · Shot / Angle Changes · TOFU → follow · effort: low · proven · source: Old proverb vs modern data — The proverb "first impressions last" vs modern halo-effect research*

**🗣 Say**

> "First impressions last" has been repeated for generations as simple advice.
> Halo effect research explains the actual mechanism: one strong early impression colors how every later interaction gets interpreted, favorably or unfavorably, regardless of its own individual merit.
> My take: this means your first client interaction deserves a disproportionate share of your preparation effort, not an equal share with every interaction after it.
> The old proverb had the conclusion right. The research explains exactly why.

#### 386. The Actual Math Behind Whether a Market Is Worth Entering

*2034-02-22 · authority · authority · Framework / Formula / Acronym · Whiteboard Format · BOFU → manychat · effort: high · proven · topic: Market Entry & Business Consulting · segment: The Math Behind It*

**🗣 Say**

> Here's the real math, not the gut feeling.
> Take total addressable market, multiply by realistic reachable share given your channels -- usually 2 to 5%, not the optimistic 20% founders assume.
> Subtract estimated entry cost, including the regulatory timeline's carrying cost, not only the marketing spend.
> Divide by 3 years to get a realistic annual return, and compare that against what the same capital could earn staying in your current market.
> If the new-market number doesn't clearly beat the current-market number, the excitement isn't enough reason to enter.
> Comment "MATH" and I'll DM you the actual spreadsheet.

**🗣 Say**

#### 467. The Framework for Building a Unit Economics Model From Scratch

*2035-09-12 · authority · authority · Framework / Formula / Acronym · Whiteboard Format · BOFU → manychat · effort: high · proven · topic: Financial Modeling & Unit Economics*

**🗣 Say**

> Most founders never build a real unit economics model until an investor asks for one. Here's how to build it properly the first time.
> Step 1: calculate fully-loaded acquisition cost per customer -- every dollar spent to win them, not only ad spend.
> Step 2: calculate delivery cost per customer -- what it actually costs to fulfill, support, and retain them.
> Step 3: calculate expected customer lifetime value based on real retention data, not an optimistic guess.
> Step 4: subtract steps 1 and 2 from step 3 -- that single number tells you more about the business than any revenue chart.

#### 507. The Framework for Building a Cash Buffer That Actually Protects the Business

**🗣 Say**

> Most founders know they should have a cash buffer. Few have a real plan for building and protecting one.

#### 791. The Framework for Building Investor Relationships Before You Need to Raise

*2041-11-27 · authority · authority · Framework / Formula / Acronym · Whiteboard Format · BOFU → manychat · effort: high · proven · topic: Fundraising & Investor Relations*

> Step 1: identify 10-15 investors whose focus genuinely fits your stage and space, not a generic list.

#### 917. The Framework for Moving From Hourly to Value-Based Pricing ⚠

*2044-04-27 · authority · authority · Framework / Formula / Acronym · Whiteboard Format · BOFU → manychat · effort: high · proven · topic: Pricing Strategy & Value-Based Fees*

| 2 | body | Mistake 1: quoting before you scope the problem | I lost a $12K deal doing exactly this in year one. |
| 3 | body | Mistake 2: pricing by the hour, not the outcome | Hourly caps your upside at your own ceiling. |
| 4 | body | Mistake 3: one flat price for every market | A Lagos entry and a Dubai entry carry different risk. |
| 5 | body | Mistake 4: no anchor tier in the proposal | Show 3 options or they anchor on the cheapest. |
| 6 | body | Mistake 5: discounting the second they hesitate | Hesitation usually means unclear value, not high price. |
| 7 | body | Mistake 6: no kill fee clause for scope changes | Scope always expands — protect the first 20 hours. |
| 8 | body | Mistake 7: never repricing after year one | I 3x'd my retainer between client 5 and client 25. |

### C15. How to Write a Proposal Clients Actually Sign

*Batch 1 · tutorial · authority/educational · MOFU → save · topic: Proposal Writing · segment: Framework Breakdown · background: whiteboard*

**Design:** Whiteboard with a sticky-note style layout, one note per proposal section.

| # | Role | Headline | Supporting text |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | hook | How to write a proposal clients sign fast | The 7-section structure I never deviate from. |
| 2 | body | Section 1: restate their problem, in their words | They need to feel heard before they read a plan. |
| 3 | body | Section 2: show the cost of doing nothing | Urgency belongs in the proposal, not just the call. |
| 4 | body | Section 3: lay out 3 pricing tiers, not one | A middle tier anchors the decision toward yes. |
| 5 | body | Section 4: include a clear timeline with milestones | Vague timelines read as vague thinking. |
| 6 | body | Section 5: add 2 relevant case studies, not 10 | Relevance beats volume every time. |
| 7 | body | Section 6: state exactly what happens after signing | Remove every bit of post-signature uncertainty. |
| 8 | body | Section 7: a deadline on the proposal itself | No deadline means no urgency to decide. |

### C89. How I Build Proposals Clients Actually Say Yes To

| 3 | body | Step 2: Name the exact market risk they're worried about |  |
| 4 | body | Step 3: Show a comparable result, not a generic case study |  |

| 6 | body | Step 5: Price phase one small enough to be a low-risk yes |  |
| 7 | body | Step 6: Attach a timeline with dates, not just durations |  |
| 8 | body | Step 7: Name what happens if they do nothing |  |
| 9 | body | Step 8: Put the next step on the same page as the price |  |
